transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start: 09:00 PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Priya, Ethan, Sofia

Summary: quick internal sync on Q4 roadmap items, launch readiness checklist, incident review notes from last week's perf regression, and final owners for next steps. focus areas: dedicated vs hosted perf, kv cache flakiness, VPC/KMS compliance items, canary windows and rollback strategies.

Topics:
- Launch readiness checklist review
- Incident review: perf regression and mitigations
- Dedicated pool smoke + quantization plan
- Security/compliance items (VPC, KMS, SOC2 artifacts)
- Rollout plan + canary thresholds

Transcript:
[09:00] Maya: okay, uh, thanks everyone for jumping on. I wanna run through the launch checklist and the open items from the incident last week. Carlos, can you start with the perf regression summary?
[09:01] Carlos: yeah, sure. So, um, last Tuesday we saw a tail latency spike on dedicated pool A, roughly 99.9th increased from 320ms to about 1.1s for a subset of, eh, requests that had long sequences and KV cache warm-up. The stack trace pointed to a kernel fallback on the newer kernel build which, um, caused excessive mem copies. We rolled forward a quick config change and that helped but we still see intermittent spikes.
[09:03] Priya: just to add, the disk I/O on that node also spiked, which made me suspect our checkpointing was contending; could be a compaction timing issue with the cache store. I opened a ticket, but we need a short-term mitigation for launch.
[09:04] Ethan: right, so mitigation options we discussed: 1) pinning the older kernel build for the affected pool, 2) forcing aggressive KV cache warming for long sequences, or 3) temporarily routing long-sequence traffic to hosted cluster fallback. each has pros/cons: pinning helps but loses perf improvements; warm-up increases cost; routing to hosted impacts data isolation.
[09:05] Maya: yep, and for launch we need predictability. I think we should avoid routing to hosted unless absolutely necessary. Priya, what would it take to pin for the next week while we finish the kernel fix?
[09:06] Priya: minimal ops effort, basically a config flag plus a rollout window. we'll need to get SRE approval for the change and update our runbook. I can own it.
[09:06] Maya: okay, Priya owns pinning. Ethan, you'll run a smoke to ensure pinning actually removes the spikes?
[09:07] Ethan: yep, I'll run an end-to-end smoke on the dedicated staging pool including the sequence distribution from the regression tests. I'll include batching and quantization variants in the run.
[09:08] Sofia: quick Q - if we pin, does that affect our recommended quantization profile? I recall that some kernels had better support for 4-bit int8 path.
[09:09] Carlos: good point. The pinned kernel doesn't have the optimized int4 path, so quantization gains might be smaller; we should document delta for cost modeling. I'll add a short bench.
[09:10] Maya: ok add that to the checklist. next, rollout plan. Carlos, what's the current canary plan?
[09:11] Carlos: proposed canary is 5% for 24 hours, then 25% for 12 hours, then 100%. We also have the automatic fallback policy to switch to a compatible model variant if error rate crosses 1.5% or P95 latency exceeds 600ms. We need a firm rollback playbook with owners.
[09:12] Ethan: small note, the auto-fallback ties into our routing layer; it might route to a different model architecture that has slightly different outputs — need to flag for product/QA.
[09:13] Maya: ok we'll add QA sign-off before canary. Sofia, can you own QA gating?
[09:14] Sofia: yes, happy to. I'll create the QA checklist and tie it to sample prompts for semantic regression checks.
[09:15] Priya: on compliance side, we need VPC peering validated across both primary and DR regions; also KMS rotation for the keys used in dedicated is scheduled next week which could interact with service restarts. We need to confirm zero-downtime rotation steps.
[09:16] Maya: do we have any outstanding SOC2 evidence items?
[09:16] Priya: there are two docs pending: change-control evidence for the kernel pin, and an updated incident postmortem with RCA. I'll pull those into the artifacts repo.
[09:17] Carlos: I also wanna flag that our cost model assumptions changed with the quantization profiles; if the pinned kernel reduces quant benefits we'll see an estimated 8-12% higher per-token cost on heavy workloads. We should surface that to finance.
[09:18] Maya: noted. Sofia, can you add a short note for finance?
[09:18] Sofia: yup.
[09:19] [09:19] Ethan: quick technical detail — the KV cache behavior: when sequence length distribution shifts, we observed increased cache misses. some of that may be due to tokenization differences across model variants, plus our prefix cache invalidation logic is a bit conservative. we could tune TTLs.
[09:21] Carlos: also worth calling out that the batcher sometimes creates larger micro-batches for small requests when the backlog accumulates, which inflates latency; that's expected but we can tune batching threshold for launch traffic shape.
[09:22] Maya: let's capture tuning knobs and owners. For launch triage: pin kernel (Priya), run smoke (Ethan), bench quantization delta (Carlos), QA sign-off (Sofia), update riser for finance (Sofia).
[09:23] Priya: about the KMS rotation — the key rotation plan is automated but we need to confirm our HSM integration for private deployments too; I will confirm with infra team and update the runbook.
[09:24] Maya: good. Incident review quick RCA bullet points?
[09:25] Ethan: temp summary - kernel fallback triggered due to new kernel edge-case on attention kernel, caused mem copies, led to increased latency and disk I/O pressure. mitigations: revert/pin kernel, patch attention kernel code, adjust cache compaction.
[09:26] Carlos: request that we add a test to our CI that simulates the long sequence KV cache warm path, so we catch regressions earlier.
[09:27] Maya: add to backlog. who will own?
[09:27] Ethan: I'll own the CI test.
[09:28] Sofia: on the launch checklist, we have a few cross-team approval gates: security sign-off, SRE readiness, product QA, and executive go/no-go. timeline looks tight; do we have a firm date for exec review?
[09:29] Maya: I proposed 2026-12-27 for exec readout to allow a week of stabilization. we need final artifacts by 12/24 ideally.
[09:30] Priya: holiday schedule caveat — some infra folks are OOO 12/24-12/26. we should plan handoffs.
[09:31] Carlos: for canary thresholds, let's document both metric thresholds and manual checkpoints: error rate, P95, end-to-end throughput, and sample output diffs. we should have automated alerts for semantic regression via our eval harness.
[09:32] Maya: good. Also, quick note on routing and fallback — ensure data residency constraints are respected if we consider routing to hosted fallback; we can't send EU data to US host. Priya?
[09:33] Priya: correct, we need region-aware fallback policies. our policy engine supports that but we need to test the policy paths.
[09:34] Ethan: I'll add region-aware smoke tests to the smoke plan.
[09:35] Maya: anything else on launch readiness?
[09:36] Sofia: just one ask — update the owner matrix with backups for each owner in case of PTO. I can draft that.
[09:37] Maya: please do. All right, moving to postmortem follow-up items — Carlos, can you summarize the timeline and RCA we should publish?
[09:38] Carlos: timeline: 12/14 regression start, 12/15 detection, 12/15 mitigated via config, 12/16 root cause analysis started, 12/18 identified kernel edge-case. RCA: kernel fallback + KV cache compaction causing I/O pressure. Action items as discussed.
[09:39] Maya: good. Let's recap owners and due dates.
[09:40] [short silence/background keyboard clacking]
[09:41] Maya: recap: Priya pins kernel on affected pool (due 12/22), Ethan smoke tests and CI test (due 12/23), Carlos bench quantization deltas and write CI sim (due 12/23), Sofia QA checklist + finance note + backup owner matrix (due 12/22), Maya will compile launch checklist and share with execs (due 12/22).
[09:43] Carlos: small note — let's schedule a quick follow-up on 12/23 to confirm canary thresholds before the 12/27 exec readout.
[09:44] Maya: scheduled. I'll send calendar invite after this call.
[09:44] Priya: also I'll upload SOC2 evidence and change-control docs to the artifacts repo once the kernel pin is approved.
[09:45] Maya: awesome. any gotchas?
[09:46] Ethan: one more, the quantization bench should include both 8-bit and 4-bit variants, and record quality deltas on our eval suite so product can sign off.
[09:47] Sofia: noted. I'll coordinate with product QA.
[09:48] Maya: okay thanks folks. thanks for the quick sync. I'll follow up with the invite and checklist.
